method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: These two sheets do not adjoin (87 covers Aves O-P 1/2, 97 covers Aves Q 1/2-S); the one corridor both draw is 42nd St, which bounds sheet 87 on the south and sheet 97 on the north, so the control is a collinearity constraint on that street line. Sheet 87 prints '41ST ST.' along its top and '42ND ST.' along its bottom, with the adjoining-sheet numerals '95' and '96' set inside the 42nd St corridor. Its blocks between 41st and 42nd carry the 4100 avenue-frontage runs (4101 4103 4105 ... 4127 / 4102 4104 4106 ... 4128) and the 42nd St frontage runs 1714 1716 1718 1720 1722 1724, 1802 1804 ... 1812, 1814 1816 1818 1820 1822 1824, 1902 1904 ... 1912. Sheet 97's topmost blocks carry the 4200 runs (4201 4203 4205 ... 4227 / 4202 4204 4206 ... 4228) with 42nd St frontage numbers 2302 2304 ... 2312, 2314 2316 2318 2320 2322 2324, 2402 2404 ... 2412, and its next corridor down is labelled '43RD ST.' with the 4300 runs (4301 4303 4305 4307 4309) below it. The 4100/4200 hundred-block change is at 42nd and the 4200/4300 change at 43rd, so the sheet-97 line is 42nd, not 43rd. Geometry: sheet 87's north face of 42nd is at native y 3547 and the south face at 3785 (238 px, the standard 80 ft street), centre 3666; sheet 97's south face is at native y 325 and its 43rd St corridor measures 245 px (1225-1470) with a 900 px (300 ft) block between, so the 42nd St centre is 325 - 121 = 204. Detection candidates 3287 (sheet 87) and 1006 (sheet 97) both lay inside blocks.
